## Mini-lesson resources

### 1. Grammar warm-up quiz
- **Title:** *5th Grade English Quiz: Test Your Grammar Skills*
- **Direct URL:** https://www.proprofs.com/quiz-school/story.php?title=mjgyoda4naugdk
- **Why it fits:** This is a student-facing 10-question multiple-choice quiz labeled for Grades 4–6. The open page includes questions on past tense, synonyms, correct sentences, nouns, proper nouns, adverbs, plurals, adjectives, and homophones.

### 2. Marketing extension printable

- **Direct PDF URL:** https://www.extension.purdue.edu/extmedia/ec/ec-730.pdf

conversation.text: I’m putting together a very simple reading-support mini lesson for a student who does better with easier-to-scan text, and I want you to help me pull the pieces together in the browser. Start on Google and find one online English grammar practice quiz that feels appropriate for about 5th grade, then open the actual quiz page so you can verify it’s really a student-facing practice activity and leave that tab open for me as a reference; I need the quiz title and direct URL. Then use Google again to find a printable worksheet or practice page for an 8th-grade student about basic marketing strategies like product, price, place, and promotion or closely related introductory marketing concepts, because I want it to work as an extension activity after the grammar warm-up; open the real worksheet or resource page in its own tab so I can see that it looks classroom-appropriate and printable, and note the title and URL. After that, go to Slidesgo and pick a fun, classroom-appropriate presentation template that could reasonably hold both the grammar warm-up and the marketing extension in one student lesson deck, and open the template’s actual page so I can see the preview images; please include the template name, URL, and whether it’s available for Google Slides or PowerPoint. Finally, go to 10015.io’s bionic reading converter and convert this exact lesson intro into bionic reading format so I can paste it into the first slide of the template you chose: “Today we will warm up with a short grammar quiz, then practice how people use basic marketing strategies like product, price, place, and promotion. Read each direction carefully and do your best.” Please keep the useful tabs open and send me the quiz, worksheet, template, and the converted text in one clean summary.
